external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
external_entities.rationale: External user or application submitting transactions - no authentication or verification of identity. Anyone can submit transactions with arbitrary gas limits.
external_entities.validation_required: Must validate gasLimit against 16,777,216 cap before accepting into mempool

external_entities.name: Peer Network Node
external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and can be malicious or compromised. Blocks received may contain invalid transactions.
external_entities.validation_required: Must validate all transaction gas limits in received blocks against cap

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled as attacker attempting DoS via high-gas transactions. Must never be trusted.
external_entities.validation_required: Gas cap enforcement is the security control to mitigate this threat

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Transaction data is completely untrusted. Gas limit validation is critical security control.
Block data from peers must be validated. Invalid blocks should be rejected and peer may be penalized.
Security boundary specifically designed to reject attacker input via gas cap enforcement.

external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
external_entities.rationale: External application or user querying historical data via RPC. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints.
external_entities.validation_required: Block identifiers should be validated. System must handle data unavailability gracefully.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: RPC requests are untrusted. Client may request invalid or unavailable data. System must validate requests and return appropriate errors.

misclassified_entities.name: Caller Contract
misclassified_entities.reason: This entity represents a contract within the EVM execution context that initiated a STATICCALL. It is an internal EVM component, not an external entity outside the system boundary. The calling contract operates within the same trust domain as the EVM execution environment.
misclassified_entities.correct_classification: Internal EVM component - contract code execution within the same transaction context

coverage_analysis.note: No true external entities exist in this specification. The one listed entity (EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT) is misclassified as it represents internal EVM contract interactions.

trust_assignments.title: EVM Arithmetic Instructions (ADD, SUB, DIV, MUL, EXP, etc.)

coverage_analysis.note: Pure computational specification with no external entity interactions. All operations occur within EVM execution context.

external_entities.name: Web Dapp
external_entities.rationale: Web application making RPC requests on behalf of user. Dapps can be malicious or compromised. No authentication mechanism.
external_entities.validation_required: Transaction parameters must be validated. RPC methods must be checked against whitelist. User must explicitly authorize transactions.

external_entities.name: End User
external_entities.rationale: Human user authorizing transactions. While the user is the ultimate authority, they can be deceived by UI spoofing or social engineering. Authorization UI must be tamper-proof.
external_entities.validation_required: User decisions are trusted once made via authentic popup, but the popup integrity is critical.

external_entities.name: Ethereum Node
external_entities.rationale: Local Ethereum node processing transactions. While typically under user control, the node could be misconfigured or compromised. The authorization mechanism should not blindly trust node responses.
external_entities.validation_required: Node availability should be verified. Connection errors should be handled gracefully.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Dapp transaction requests are untrusted. User must explicitly review and approve via popup before execution.
Iframe RPC requests are filtered against allowedMethods whitelist. Non-whitelisted methods return notAllowed error.

coverage_analysis.note: EXT-USER interacts via UI (approve/reject buttons) but has no explicit data-carrying edge in the subgraph. EXT-ETH-NODE is a destination for authorized transactions, not a source of inbound data.
